evidence.note: Before any overlay appears, the context diagram is already blurred so heavily that no label, node or legend text can be read; only faint blue/red smears and box outlines remain.
Same: the diagram and legend are an unreadable blur with nothing in focus on the slide except the title.
First insight card is crisp, white, with a soft drop shadow, clearly in focus above the blurred diagram to its right.
Three opaque cards cover almost all of the diagram; only blurred legend fragments peek out below, so the context is effectively gone.
Same: the cards hide the diagram; the remaining context is an unrecognisable haze.

rationale: The cards do hold focus clearly through shadow and contrast, so the overlay does not fight the content. But the blur is so heavy that the underlying diagram is unrecognisable even at step 0, before any overlay exists, and by step 3 the opaque cards hide it almost entirely. This matches the fail descriptor 'effects so heavy the context is lost', not the pass anchor of an overlay floating above softened but recognisable content.
